scope: Cross-cutting baseline for any app that calls an LLM: provider routing, an optional host-side LLM gateway (a local proxy that fronts a hosted model API or CLI), a local model server (e.g. Ollama), RAG through a shared vector store, streaming, sidecar agents. Apply it IN ADDITION to the app's domain baseline (nextjs.json / api.json). It does not cover Claude Code subagents or vendored third-party agent frameworks.
description: Edit `config` to match your environment. Every hostname/port below is a placeholder.

config.vector_store: Shared vector DB reached ONLY through the gateway's /rag/* endpoints (or your equivalent)

provider_routing.pattern: ONE LLM client file per app reads LLM_PROVIDER at load time and dispatches. Every code path that ends at a backend which is down must fail CLOSED and LOUDLY (clean error + health flag), never hang.
provider_routing.defaults: The compose default (`${LLM_PROVIDER:-<x>}`) is a feature toggle, the one allowed `:-` exception. Record which default each app ships and why; a default pointing at a backend that no longer exists is a finding.
provider_routing.what_routes_where: Embeddings and streaming may not be supported by every backend — branch on the stream flag and route stream:true to a backend that streams.

compose_contract.note: extra_hosts is MANDATORY on Linux containers that call a host-side service. `localhost` inside a container is the container.

headers.X-App-Name: REQUIRED on every gateway call — drives per-app metrics, allowlist policy and rate limits. Observability/policy, NOT authentication (spoofable by any local process).
headers.auth_token: Shared secret header, compared constant-time on the gateway. Treat the gateway port as a trust boundary.

gateway.policy: Per-app allowlist (models + hourly budget) with a restrictive '*' default that fails closed for unknown apps.

local_model_server.exposure: Never publish the model server port on 0.0.0.0. Reach it via a private network or host.docker.internal.
local_model_server.note: An `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:<port>`-style env is a bind inside the container's own network namespace — only a compose `ports:` entry publishes to the host.

rag.access: Apps go through ONE retrieval API (gateway /rag/* or equivalent), never the vector DB SDK directly — keeps embedding model, dimensions and collection naming consistent.
rag.chunking: Long docs are upserted with server-side chunking and stable chunk ids (<id>#<n>) so re-upsert overwrites in place
rag.dedup: Omit the id to derive a deterministic UUID from sha256(text) — same content, same point
rag.drift: Record the embed model per collection; warn on mismatch
rag.privacy: Retrieved chunks are sent to whichever model generates the answer. A collection that must not leave the machine is either search-only or paired with a local provider.
rag.backup: Scheduled snapshot of every collection with rotation, or an explicit documented backup story

llm_endpoints: Input sanitization: strip HTML, cap prompt length
Rate limit all AI endpoints (e.g. 20/min generation, 50/min search)
Never splice raw user input into a system prompt
LLM output is untrusted: validate JSON with zod/pydantic, never execute or render it unescaped
Subprocess calls with array args only (execFile / subprocess.run([...]))
Constant-time comparison for every auth token
docker: Same hardening as the domain baseline (cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, read_only, tmpfs, 127.0.0.1)
Docker socket mounts only read-only, documented as an accepted risk, never on an internet-facing service

testing: Mock every backend (local model AND gateway) for deterministic tests
Provider-routing tests: same prompt takes different code paths per LLM_PROVIDER
Gateway auth: 401 on token mismatch; allowlist 403 on a disallowed model
JSON extraction strips markdown fences and validates the schema
Backend-down test: request fails fast with a clear error, no hang
observability: Per call: provider, model, operation, latency, status (success | error | timeout | fallback), cache hit/miss
Gateway /health reports each backend's reachability; the app's health/status surfaces 'AI unavailable' instead of a spinner
Fallback counter monitored — sustained fallbacks mean quota pressure

patterns.graceful_degradation: Every AI call in try/catch with a meaningful fallback; RAG failure returns empty context
patterns.lazy_singleton: SDK clients created on first use, not at import (prevents build failures)
patterns.timeouts: Every outbound LLM call has an explicit timeout (AbortSignal.timeout / httpx timeout); a circuit breaker treats abort/timeout as a failure
patterns.circuit_breaker: e.g. 3 retries with backoff, open after 5 consecutive failures for 5 min

anti_patterns.name: Provider hardcoded
anti_patterns.fix: Single client file dispatching on LLM_PROVIDER

anti_patterns.name: Inline prompt strings everywhere
anti_patterns.fix: Typed templates in one prompts module

anti_patterns.name: No retry/timeout on LLM calls
anti_patterns.fix: Explicit timeout + bounded retry with backoff + breaker

anti_patterns.name: Blocking LLM calls in async Python
No JSON output validation
anti_patterns.fix: zod / pydantic; retry once with a stricter prompt on parse failure

anti_patterns.name: Model server port published to the host
Hosted-model SDK called directly when the architecture mandates the gateway
anti_patterns.fix: Route through the gateway — bypassing it bypasses metrics, cache, allowlist and billing controls

anti_patterns.name: Missing X-App-Name
anti_patterns.fix: Send it on every gateway call

anti_patterns.name: Streaming routed to a non-streaming backend
Sensitive collection paired with a hosted provider
anti_patterns.fix: Search-only collection, or local provider for that app

anti_patterns.name: Hardcoded model id in source
anti_patterns.fix: Read LLM_MODEL from env (alias like haiku|sonnet|opus mapped by the gateway)

anti_patterns.name: Dangling backend hostname
anti_patterns.fix: Fallback strings in code pointing at a retired container/host — flag if the compose default does not override them

deployment_checklist: Gateway URL / model / token env passthrough; token via ${VAR:?}
extra_hosts host.docker.internal:host-gateway on every service calling a host service
X-App-Name and the auth token header on every gateway call
App listed in the gateway allowlist with model + hourly budget
No direct vector-DB or hosted-model SDK imports when the gateway is mandated
Streaming paths routed to a streaming backend
Rate limiting + input sanitization on all AI endpoints
Graceful, fast failure when the backend is down

audit_checklist.check: LLM_PROVIDER dispatch exists with a documented default that points at a live backend
Gateway URL / model / token passthroughs in compose; token via ${VAR:?}
extra_hosts host.docker.internal:host-gateway present on every service that calls a host service
Every gateway call sends X-App-Name
Auth token header sent on every gateway call; gateway compares constant-time
No direct vector-DB SDK import
No direct hosted-model SDK import when the gateway is mandated
Long-doc upserts use server-side chunking
Streaming paths route to a backend that streams
Sensitive collections are search-only or paired with a local provider
Provider routing lives in one client file, not scattered
App present in the gateway allowlist with a model + hourly budget
Vector-store backup scheduled or documented
Mocks cover every backend; routing + auth-failure + backend-down tests exist
Model id read from env, not hardcoded
Model server port not published to the host
Vector DB / model server images digest-pinned and above known CVE floors
JSON output validated with zod/pydantic
Explicit timeout + breaker on every outbound LLM call; dead backend surfaces as a clean error
Rate limiting + input caps on every AI endpoint
